course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Norm production I: the comparative approach and codification

slides.title: Why compare, and what exactly
slides.text: Foljanty's exercise class opens with a question the exam likes to ask: WHY COMPARE. The answer rests on the fact that IN EUROPEAN LEGAL HISTORY THERE IS A SHARED DEVELOPMENT BUT ALSO SIGNIFICANT DIVERGENCES. Comparison then does two things: (1) IT MAKES SIMILARITIES AND DIFFERENCES VISIBLE and (2) IT INVITES US TO ANALYSE THEIR REASONS. The second step is the essential one — merely establishing that something differs is not yet knowledge. WHAT IS COMPARED: LEGAL CULTURE, that is, THE CHARACTERISTICS OF A GIVEN LEGAL ORDER IN TERMS OF HOW THE SYSTEM WORKS AND HOW IT RELATES TO SOCIETY. It includes NORMS, INSTITUTIONS, ACTORS, THEIR EXPLICIT AND TACIT KNOWLEDGE and the CONVENTIONS ABOUT HOW LAW IS PRACTISED. HOW ONE COMPARES: the concept of legal culture is broken down into OBSERVATION POINTS that are its load-bearing pillars — NORM PRODUCTION, THE LEGAL PROFESSIONS AND METHODS, CONSTITUTIONS. AUSTRIA, FRANCE AND ENGLAND are examined. AND A METHODOLOGICAL WARNING TO REMEMBER: WE ARE NOT COMPARING STATIC WHOLES BUT DYNAMIC LEGAL CULTURES — not two states of affairs, then, but two movements.

terms.def: The characteristics of a legal order in terms of how the system works and relates to society — norms, institutions, actors, their knowledge and the conventions of practice.

cards.a: Because in European legal history there is a SHARED DEVELOPMENT BUT ALSO SIGNIFICANT DIVERGENCES. Comparison 1) MAKES SIMILARITIES AND DIFFERENCES VISIBLE and 2) INVITES ANALYSIS OF THEIR REASONS — the second step is the essential one, because establishing a difference is not yet knowledge.

cards.q: What is legal culture and which observation points are compared?
cards.a: THE CHARACTERISTICS OF A LEGAL ORDER IN TERMS OF HOW THE SYSTEM WORKS AND HOW IT RELATES TO SOCIETY — it includes NORMS, INSTITUTIONS, ACTORS, their EXPLICIT AND TACIT KNOWLEDGE and the CONVENTIONS OF PRACTICE. The observation points: NORM PRODUCTION, THE LEGAL PROFESSIONS AND METHODS, CONSTITUTIONS. And the warning: WE ARE NOT COMPARING STATIC WHOLES BUT DYNAMIC LEGAL CULTURES.

slides.title: Three sources of norm production and three models
slides.text: This is the skeleton of the whole pair of exercise classes and the most valuable thing in them. NORM PRODUCTION HAS THREE SOURCES: (1) LEGISLATION — CODIFICATIONS AND STATUTE LAW as normative sources; (2) JUDICIAL DECISIONS — CASE LAW AND JUDGE-MADE LAW as the production of new norms; (3) LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP — THE CREATION OF DOCTRINE THROUGH INTERPRETATION AND SYSTEMATIZATION as a contribution to the production of new norms. Note the wording of the second and third: it is not that the court or scholarship merely discovers the law — THEY PRODUCE NEW NORMS. And to each of those sources there corresponds ONE NATIONAL MODEL in which it appears in pure form: THE FIRST MODEL — CODIFICATION (FRANCE, AUSTRIA); THE SECOND MODEL — JUDGE-MADE LAW (ENGLAND); THE THIRD MODEL — LAW AS AN ACADEMIC CREATION (GERMANY). Remember this trio together with the countries assigned to it, because it is a ready-made outline for anything on 19th-century norm production.

cards.q: Which three sources of norm production does Foljanty distinguish?
cards.a: 1) LEGISLATION — codifications and statute law. 2) JUDICIAL DECISIONS — case law and judge-made law as the PRODUCTION OF NEW NORMS. 3) LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP — the creation of DOCTRINE THROUGH INTERPRETATION AND SYSTEMATIZATION as a contribution to the production of new norms. In the second and third it is not a matter of merely discovering the law — THEY PRODUCE NEW NORMS.

cards.q: Which three national models correspond to the three sources of norm production?
cards.a: THE FIRST MODEL — CODIFICATION: FRANCE AND AUSTRIA. THE SECOND MODEL — JUDGE-MADE LAW: ENGLAND. THE THIRD MODEL — LAW AS AN ACADEMIC CREATION: GERMANY.

slides.title: Codification: why it arose and what is new about it
slides.text: WHY CODIFICATION AROSE has, according to the exercise class, two causes. (1) RATIONALISM AS A NEW PARADIGM: ABSTRACT REGULATION, SYSTEMATIZATION, ACCESSIBLE LANGUAGE. (2) THE CREATION OF A UNIFIED STATE — in AUSTRIA through enlightened absolutism, in FRANCE through post-revolutionary nation-building. From both follows the GOAL: THE HOMOGENEOUS REGULATION OF AN ENTIRE FIELD OF LAW. THE ORIGIN OF THE WORD is neat and usable: 'CODIFICATION' GOES BACK TO THE LATIN CODEX, which was ORIGINALLY WOODEN TABLETS BOUND TOGETHER — a book as against a scroll. And the definition: A LAW BOOK THAT CLAIMS TO REGULATE ITS SUBJECT COMPLETELY, SYSTEMATICALLY AND EXCLUSIVELY. THE MAIN FEATURES OF CODIFICATIONS are three and are neatly ordered by what they concern. (a) A NEW FORM OF LEGISLATION: THE CREATION OF NEW LAW, A SYSTEMATIC STRUCTURE, A CLAIM TO COMPLETENESS AND EXCLUSIVITY. (b) NEW DEMARCATIONS: A CLEAR SEPARATION OF PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAW. (c) NEW CONTENT: PRIVATE LAW AS A LAW SUBORDINATED TO THE PRIMACY OF FREEDOM. That third point is often left out, and yet it is the most important: a codification is not merely a different form of the same law but also A DIFFERENT CONTENT.

cards.q: From which two causes did codification arise and what was its goal?
cards.a: 1) RATIONALISM AS A NEW PARADIGM — abstract regulation, systematization, accessible language. 2) THE CREATION OF A UNIFIED STATE — in Austria through ENLIGHTENED ABSOLUTISM, in France through POST-REVOLUTIONARY NATION-BUILDING. The goal: THE HOMOGENEOUS REGULATION OF AN ENTIRE FIELD OF LAW.

cards.q: Which three main features does a codification have?
cards.a: a) A NEW FORM OF LEGISLATION: the creation of new law, a SYSTEMATIC STRUCTURE, a CLAIM TO COMPLETENESS AND EXCLUSIVITY. b) NEW DEMARCATIONS: A CLEAR SEPARATION OF PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAW. c) NEW CONTENT: PRIVATE LAW AS A LAW SUBORDINATED TO THE PRIMACY OF FREEDOM. The third point is often left out, and yet it is the most important: a codification is not merely a different FORM but also A DIFFERENT CONTENT.

cards.q: Where does the word 'codification' come from?
cards.a: From the Latin CODEX, which was ORIGINALLY WOODEN TABLETS BOUND TOGETHER — a BOOK as against a scroll. Hence A LAW BOOK THAT CLAIMS TO REGULATE ITS SUBJECT COMPLETELY, SYSTEMATICALLY AND EXCLUSIVELY.

slides.title: Source: the promulgation patent of the ABGB (1811)
slides.text: THE SOURCE: '…We have now resolved to promulgate this General Civil Code for all Our German hereditary lands and to order that it shall come into force on the first of January 1812. THEREBY THE COMMON LAW HITHERTO RECEIVED, THE FIRST PART OF THE CIVIL CODE PROMULGATED ON 1 NOVEMBER 1786, THE CIVIL CODE GIVEN FOR GALICIA, TOGETHER WITH ALL STATUTES AND CUSTOMS RELATING TO THE SUBJECTS OF THIS GENERAL CIVIL LAW, CEASE TO HAVE EFFECT.' THIS EXTRACT IS THE BEST EVIDENCE OF EXCLUSIVITY AS A FEATURE OF CODIFICATION, and therefore deserves analysis. Note everything that is repealed at one stroke: (1) 'THE COMMON LAW HITHERTO RECEIVED', that is, the IUS COMMUNE — the entire received Roman-law tradition ends in a single sentence; (2) THE RULER'S OWN EARLIER CODES (the Josephine of 1786, the Galician); (3) AND MOST POWERFULLY, 'ALL STATUTES AND CUSTOMS' relating to the same subject — that is, CUSTOM too, which was never promulgated and which nobody wrote down. A codification therefore repeals not merely competing texts but THE WHOLE PREVIOUS WAY IN WHICH LAW CAME INTO BEING. That is the 'exclusivity' the doctrine speaks of — and one can see that it is a hard cut, not a formality.

cards.q: What does the promulgation patent of the ABGB repeal, and why does it matter?
cards.a: It repeals at one stroke 1) 'THE COMMON LAW HITHERTO RECEIVED', that is, the IUS COMMUNE — the whole received tradition ends in a single sentence; 2) THE RULER'S OWN EARLIER CODES (Josephine 1786, Galician); 3) and most powerfully 'ALL STATUTES AND CUSTOMS' on the same subject, that is, CUSTOM too. A codification therefore repeals not merely competing TEXTS but THE WHOLE PREVIOUS WAY IN WHICH LAW CAME INTO BEING.

slides.title: The long road to the ABGB — the exact sequence
slides.text: The exercise class gives the exact sequence together with characterizations, and it is worth knowing, because the examiner asks about the steps. (1) THE CODEX THERESIANUS 1766 — BASED ON ROMAN LAW, STRONGLY CASUISTIC. That is why it did not pass: casuistry is the opposite of the abstract regulation codification aims at. (2) HORTEN'S DRAFT 1774 — a reworking of the Theresianum into a more concise form. (3) THE GENERAL CIVIL CODE, PART I, that is, the JOSEPHINE CODE, 1786 — IT CONTAINS ONLY THE LAW OF PERSONS AND FAMILY AND MATRIMONIAL PROPERTY LAW. Only the first part; the rest was never finished. (4) THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSION FOR THE GENERAL CIVIL CODE LED BY KARL ANTON VON MARTINI (1726–1800), later by his pupil FRANZ VON ZEILLER (1751–1828). (5) THE CIVIL CODE FOR GALICIA 1797/98 — PUT INTO FORCE IN WEST AND EAST GALICIA AND IN BUKOVINA. That is the trial run: newly acquired lands served as a laboratory. (6) THE GENERAL CIVIL CODE (ABGB) 1811. THE WHOLE ROAD THEREFORE TOOK FIFTY-FIVE YEARS AND INVOLVED TWO FAILED ATTEMPTS, ONE UNFINISHED PART AND ONE TRIAL RUN — a good answer to the question why codifications take so long.

cards.q: What was the exact sequence of steps to the ABGB?
cards.a: 1766 THE CODEX THERESIANUS (based on Roman law, STRONGLY CASUISTIC — which is why it failed). 1774 HORTEN'S DRAFT. 1786 THE JOSEPHINE CODE as PART I (only the law of persons, family and matrimonial property). The commission led by MARTINI (1726–1800), then ZEILLER (1751–1828). 1797/98 THE CODE FOR GALICIA (in force in West and East Galicia and Bukovina — the trial run). 1811 THE ABGB.

cards.q: Why did the road to the ABGB take so long?
cards.a: It took FIFTY-FIVE YEARS and involved TWO FAILED ATTEMPTS (the Theresianum for its casuistry, Horten's draft), ONE UNFINISHED PART (the Josephine Code) and ONE TRIAL RUN (the Galician code in the newly acquired lands).

slides.title: Référé législatif, § 7 and § 8 ABGB
slides.text: Here the exercise class gives a threefold distinction that is easy to confuse in the exam and therefore deserves care. THE PROBLEM: CODIFICATIONS USED TO BE ACCOMPANIED BY THE 'RÉFÉRÉ LÉGISLATIF' — THE INTERPRETATION AND FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF THE LAW BELONGS TO THE LEGISLATOR ALONE; THE JUDGE IS BOUND. THE AUSTRIAN DEVELOPMENT: THE CODEX THERESIANUS (1766) AND THE JOSEPHINE CODE (1786) STILL CONTAIN IT. THE WEST GALICIAN CODE (1797) AND THE ABGB (1811) NO LONGER DO. AND THE ABGB GOES FURTHER STILL: IT EXPRESSLY GIVES THE JUDGE THE POWER TO DECIDE CASES WHERE NEITHER THE WORDING NOR THE NATURAL MEANING OF THE STATUTE HELPS. § 7 ABGB: 'If a case at law cannot be decided either from the words or from the natural meaning of a statute, REGARD MUST BE HAD TO SIMILAR CASES DEFINITELY DECIDED IN THE STATUTES AND TO THE GROUNDS OF OTHER RELATED STATUTES. IF THE CASE STILL REMAINS DOUBTFUL, IT MUST BE DECIDED ACCORDING TO THE NATURAL PRINCIPLES OF LAW, having regard to the circumstances carefully collected and maturely considered.' AND NOW THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: THE RÉFÉRÉ LÉGISLATIF MUST BE DISTINGUISHED FROM AUTHENTIC INTERPRETATION. Authentic interpretation means that ONLY THE LEGISLATOR MAY INTERPRET A STATUTE IN A GENERALLY BINDING WAY — this remains, and is governed by § 8 ABGB. INTERPRETATION OF THE CODIFICATION BY THE COURTS IS THEREFORE PERMITTED, BUT ITS RESULT IS NOT GENERALLY BINDING; IT MATTERS ONLY FOR THE INDIVIDUAL CASE. § 8 adds that such an explanation by the legislator APPLIES TO ALL CASES NOT YET DECIDED, unless the legislator himself provides that it does not extend to transactions and rights arising before the explanation.

terms.def: Interpretation of a statute in a generally binding way, which only the legislator may give (§ 8 ABGB).

cards.q: How did the référé législatif develop in the Austrian codifications?
cards.a: THE CODEX THERESIANUS (1766) AND THE JOSEPHINE CODE (1786) STILL CONTAIN IT. THE WEST GALICIAN CODE (1797) AND THE ABGB (1811) NO LONGER DO — and the ABGB goes further still: IT EXPRESSLY GIVES THE JUDGE THE POWER TO DECIDE WHERE NEITHER THE WORDING NOR THE NATURAL MEANING OF THE STATUTE HELPS.

cards.q: What is the difference between the référé législatif and authentic interpretation?
cards.a: The RÉFÉRÉ LÉGISLATIF means that THE JUDGE MAY NOT INTERPRET AT ALL and must ask the legislator — this the ABGB abandoned. AUTHENTIC INTERPRETATION means that ONLY THE LEGISLATOR MAY INTERPRET A STATUTE IN A GENERALLY BINDING WAY (§ 8 ABGB) — this remains. INTERPRETATION BY THE COURTS IS THEREFORE PERMITTED, BUT ITS RESULT IS NOT GENERALLY BINDING, ONLY FOR THE INDIVIDUAL CASE.

cards.q: What procedure does § 7 ABGB prescribe for gaps?
cards.a: Where the case cannot be decided from the words or the natural meaning of the statute: 1) HAVE REGARD TO SIMILAR CASES DEFINITELY DECIDED IN THE STATUTES; 2) TO THE GROUNDS OF OTHER RELATED STATUTES; 3) if the case still remains doubtful, DECIDE ACCORDING TO THE NATURAL PRINCIPLES OF LAW, having regard to the circumstances carefully collected and maturely considered.
